name: Front Lower Links (Lateral LCA + Radius/Tension Rod)
description: The Gen 6 front is a double-pivot MacPherson strut: instead of one lower A-arm, two separate aluminum links each carry their own ball joint at the knuckle. The lateral 'lower control arm' reacts mainly side loads; the forward-running 'radius rod' (GM: front lower control link; aftermarket: tension rod / caster rod) reacts braking/longitudinal loads and sets caster. Both inner pivots bolt to the front cradle with torque-to-yield bolts.

components.name: Front lower control arm (lateral link) with ball joint
components.description: Forged aluminum lateral link from the cradle out to the bottom of the knuckle. Its inner end has a rubber bushing (horizontal through-bolt into the cradle) and its outer end an integral tapered-stud ball joint that bolts into the knuckle with a 21 mm nut. Its length sets static camber in the double-pivot design; adjustable race arms add camber and roll-center correction.
components.location: Inner pivot approx (x 0.04, y 0.20, z +/-0.36) on the cradle to ball joint approx (x 0.03, y 0.17, z +/-0.71).

factory.name: GM aluminum front lower control arm (ball joint integral)
factory.notes: Same arm across V6 to ZL1 per owner reports; no verified GM part number found.

raceOptions.name: SPL Parts FLCA CAM6 adjustable front lower control arms
raceOptions.notes: Billet 6061-T6 arm with chromoly double adjuster; camber/track width adjustable (up to approx 4.3 deg depending on ride height); roll-center correction spacers; FK spherical bearings. Knuckle bolt hole must be slightly clearanced.

raceOptions.name: BMR BK071 front LCA spherical bearing kit
raceOptions.notes: Presses a 3/4 in spherical bearing in a CNC cup into the factory arm in place of the rubber bushing.

hardware.item: Front lower control link bolt - control arm (inner pivot to cradle)
hardware.spec: M12 class flange bolt (18 mm hex) + nut; GM P/N 11611268
hardware.torqueSequence: First pass 100 N·m (74 lb ft), final pass +90-105 deg; torque with suspension at normal ride height
hardware.notes: Torquing a rubber-bushed pivot at full droop preloads the bushing - set the car at ride height (or jack the knuckle to ride height) before final torque.

hardware.item: Lower control arm ball stud nut (to knuckle)
hardware.torqueSequence: First pass 40 N·m (30 lb ft), then final pass +120–135° (angle gauge). GM tightens the link's inner bolt (100 N·m + 90–105°) before this nut. Hold the stud with a hex key if it spins.
hardware.tool: 21 mm deep socket; hold stud with hex key if it spins
hardware.notes: Value NOT verified against GM SI - confirm before use. Separate the taper with a brass hammer / ball joint separator, never by hammering the stud threads. [2026-10 check] CORRECTED: was 'secondary source 80 ft-lb (108 N·m) + 90°' (chevy-specs). GM calls this lateral link the 'front lower control rear link' (French text: 'bras transversal inférieur arrière'), and its knuckle nut the 'Steering Knuckle Nut': 40 N·m + 120–135°. Same value in GM Chevrolet Performance SC1 kit sheets 84242387 (2016) and 84401189 (2017), and in the 1LE kit sheet 84233246 (GM doc ID 4508965, 2024 SI print). TightTorque also lists 'steering knuckle nut, first pass 40 N·m'.

installNotes: Install inner bolt from the factory direction; leave loose until ride height.
Seat ball stud taper clean and dry in the knuckle, install new nut and torque.
Final-torque inner TTY bolt at ride height with new bolt.
inspection: Check ball joint for play and boot tears.
Inspect aluminum arm for curb/impact damage (bent arms change camber).
Check witness marks on inner bolt.

components.name: Front radius rod (tension/caster rod, front lower control link) with ball joint
components.description: Aluminum link running forward from its ball joint at the bottom of the knuckle to a large bushing at the front of the cradle. It carries braking (tension) and acceleration loads and sets caster; bushing compliance lets caster and toe change under braking. On ZL1 cars with the extra front coolers, the cooler may need to be unbolted to remove the inner bolt.
components.location: Ball joint approx (x -0.03, y 0.18, z +/-0.70) forward to inner pivot approx (x -0.38, y 0.22, z +/-0.42) at the cradle front.

factory.name: GM aluminum front radius rod (front lower control link)
factory.notes: BMR and SPL list the same rod for 2016-2024 Camaro and 2015-2019 CTS-V.

raceOptions.name: SPL Parts TR CAM6 adjustable front tension rods
raceOptions.notes: Billet 2024 aluminum, FK PTFE rod ends; wide caster adjustment (equalize L/R); anti-dive tuning with spacers; knuckle hole needs slight clearancing for 5/8 in SHCS.

raceOptions.name: BMR FLC363 double-adjustable front arms (replace radius rods)
raceOptions.notes: 1 in DOM tube with Teflon-lined rod ends; chrome rod end to chassis, black rod end to spindle. Chassis bolt 74 ft-lb + 90-105 deg (factory bolt), spindle stud 94 ft-lb.

raceOptions.name: BMR BK070 radius rod spherical bearing kit (1 in)
raceOptions.notes: Keeps factory rod; bearing in billet cup.

raceOptions.name: SPL CRB CAM6 adjustable caster rod monoball bushings
raceOptions.notes: 1 in FK bearings with offset spacers for caster adjustment (listing states +/-2 deg in description, +/-4 deg in features - confirm).

hardware.item: Front lower control link bolt - radius rod (inner pivot to cradle)
hardware.spec: M12 class flange bolt (18 mm hex) + nut; GM P/N 11610915
hardware.torqueSequence: First pass 100 N·m (74 lb ft), final pass +90-105 deg, at ride height
hardware.notes: Access requires removing lower splash shields; on cars with the extra cooler, unbolt the cooler to withdraw the bolt. BMR installs this bolt from the back side with their bearing kit.

hardware.item: Radius rod ball stud nut (to knuckle)
hardware.torque: Factory link: 30 ft-lb (40 N·m) first pass + 120–135° (GM steering knuckle nut). BMR FLC363 arm: 94 ft-lb (127 N·m) per BMR.
hardware.notes: Factory value not verified in available sources. [2026-10 check] GM kit sheets give 40 N·m + 120–135° for the 'Steering Knuckle Nut' only in the rear-link (lateral arm) procedure. TightTorque (GM 2016–18 SI) lists one 'steering knuckle nut' spec (40 N·m first pass), and an ATS (Alpha) owner-quoted SI gives 40 N·m + 120°, so the same nut spec very likely applies to the front link (radius rod). Not seen in a GM front-link procedure, so confirm in GM SI. Was 'See GM SI'.
hardware.torqueSequence: Factory link: 40 N·m (30 lb ft), then +120–135°. BMR FLC363: single torque 94 ft-lb on the BMR-supplied stud and nut.

installNotes: Remove front splash shields (7 mm, 10 mm and T15 fasteners plus push clips) for access.
Final torque inner TTY bolt at ride height.
Re-check caster after any rod/bushing change.
inspection: Check bushing/bearing for play and the ball joint boot.
Check rod for bending after curb strikes (caster/toe change).

components.name: Front radius rod bushing (cradle end)
components.description: Large rubber bushing at the front (cradle) end of the radius rod. Its compliance is tuned for ride comfort and lets the wheel move rearward under braking - which changes caster and toe. Replacing it with a spherical bearing (BMR BK070, SPL CRB CAM6) is one of the most effective front-end upgrades for consistent braking feel.
components.location: Front of cradle, approx (x -0.38, y 0.22, z +/-0.42).

raceOptions.name: BMR BK070 (1 in spherical in 6061 cup)

installNotes: Press out factory bushing with a press; install bearing cup, snap ring and spacers.
inspection: Check for bearing play and liner wear.

components.name: Front lower ball joints (two per side)
components.description: Each front lower link has its own ball joint at the knuckle, which creates the 'virtual' lower pivot of the double-pivot strut (steering axis passes through the instantaneous intersection of the two links, reducing scrub radius). On factory links the ball joints are integral to the link; race links use spherical rod ends or high-misalignment bearings.
components.location: Bottom of each knuckle, approx (x -0.03 and 0.03, y 0.17-0.18, z +/-0.70).

factory.name: Integral ball joints in GM aluminum links

installNotes: Clean tapers (no grease/anti-seize) before installing studs.
inspection: Check for radial/axial play with the wheel unloaded; check boots.
